free_energy_functional.key_insight: For γ < γ_c, F[φ] is convex with unique minimum (uniform phase). For γ > γ_c, the nonlocal term -(γ/2)Σ(φ-φ')²K makes F[φ] non-convex, creating multiple local minima that correspond to distinct core patterns. The constraint φ ≥ 0 further restricts the feasible set.

nonlocal_ks.free_energy_type: convex for γ < γ_c, non-convex for γ > γ_c

key_insight: The nonlocal KS free energy is convex for γ < γ_c (uniform phase) and non-convex for γ > γ_c (ordered phase). The non-convexity arises from the nonlocal attraction term -(γ/2)Σ(φ-φ')²K, which favors spatial heterogeneity. The constraint φ ≥ 0 further restricts the feasible set, creating an obstacle problem structure. This is fundamentally different from the local KS, where the cubic chemotaxis term provides intrinsic nonlinear saturation.
